summary: The metric closure MST approach scored 86.95/100, dramatically outperforming the full MST+prune baseline (62.15/100). The algorithm is near-optimal on 4 of 10 test cases (perfect 10.0), but leaves ~13 points on the table across the remaining 6 cases. The next iteration should focus on improving relay utilization through subgraph enrichment and local search techniques.
key_points: CONFIRMED: Metric closure MST (86.95) beats full MST+prune (62.15) by 24.8 points, validating that separating connectivity decisions from relay assignment is the key algorithmic insight for this Steiner tree variant.

The scoring formula is linear interpolation between MST cost and MST×8/9 — achieving full marks requires saving ~11% of MST cost via relays. Four test cases already hit this threshold; six remain below.

Critical constraint discovered: relay-to-relay (C-C) edges are forbidden, making relay-mediated paths exactly 2-hop (robot→relay→robot). This makes the metric closure computation exact, not approximate.
Weakest tests: test1 (N=10,K=10, score 6.99) and test2 (N=100,K=10, score 1.48) have few relays relative to edges; tests 3,5,8,10 (N=K=1500) score 9.3-9.9, suggesting relay coverage gaps.

Several improvement attempts failed in iteration 1: top-K relay reconstruction hurt score (75.99), hub expansion was neutral, and relay replacement had no effect — indicating that naive augmentation of the subgraph degrades tree quality.

NEXT ITERATION should investigate: (1) more careful subgraph enrichment — add only relays that improve specific bottleneck MST edges rather than blanket top-K; (2) post-MST local search swapping relay assignments edge-by-edge; (3) KD-tree or spatial indexing to efficiently find best relay for each edge during iterative improvement passes.
